name: Speed Import
description: The shortest path from a live website to a live Fluid storefront: brand, catalog, home, shop, product, publish. One model — Grok 4.5 — end to end, no QA turns, nothing that can stop the run. Deliberately skips the onboarding form, content and collection import, media and UGC, and storefront QA; the handoff says so explicitly. Use Streamlined Onboard & Launch when the company needs to actually launch.

steps.name: Map the source catalog
steps.prompt:
Build the product source manifest. Call run_skill("fluid-product-admin-import") and follow its catalog completion contract. Read-only against Fluid.

Discovery is a union of sitemap, any structured catalog API, and every collection pagination followed to its end — then fetch each unique PDP for real fields: identity, title, description, price, variants, images, collection membership.

Speed matters here, completeness matters more: a product you never discovered is a product the store cannot sell. But do not re-verify what you already have.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { manifest_path, products, variants, collections, unresolved: [...] }.

steps.name: Capture the source site
steps.prompt:
Capture the source home page once so the page steps build from evidence rather than re-crawling. Call run_skill("themes/theme-source-inventory") and follow it.

Home in full at desktop and at 390 wide, formats ["html", "rawHtml", "screenshot"], capturePageEvidence: true — that retains the site's own CSS labelled by origin and resolved computed styles for every text landmark. Plus a route inventory: the canonical URL for shop, one product, and the main content pages. Do not deep-capture every route.

Write clone-manifest.json with the route map and evidence paths.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { routes: {...}, evidence: {...} }.

steps.name: Publish the theme
steps.prompt:
Publish the built theme.

1. Confirm no scaffold filler survived in the touched templates — placeholder names and starter-theme copy both count.
2. Record the development theme id and the release target id; they are not the same theme.
3. Push and activate the release target, then GET /api/application_themes/active and confirm the active id is the one you pushed.
4. Load the live home URL and one product route and confirm each returns 200 with a real body.

Publish even if a page step left findings; carry them into your output.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { release_theme_id, active_theme_id, live_url, routes_checked: [{route, status}], carried_findings: [...] }.

steps.name: What landed, and what needs you
steps.prompt:
Write the handoff. Pull each step's STEP_OUTPUT; re-do nothing.

Lead with the live storefront URL and one honest sentence on whether this company could take an order today. Then: what is live, with counts; what is blocking, each with the single action that clears it; and what this run deliberately skipped — business profile and onboarding form, collections and content pages, media and UGC, and any broad storefront QA. Those are not failures, they are the trade this workflow makes for speed, and the operator needs to know they are outstanding.

Counts, routes, and ids — not adjectives.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { live_url, can_take_an_order: true|false, live: {...}, blocking: [...], not_attempted: [...] }.
